answer: Stop sybils with privacy-preserving biometric uniqueness: each agent proves one human body stands behind it, without revealing who. To join, an agent (1) scans one iris at a certified kiosk, (2) posts a zero-knowledge proof that its hash is new, (3) the network stores only the hash, never the scan, and (4) a duplicate hash is rejected and the kiosk flagged. Faking 10,000 agents needs 10,000 real irises, $200 scanners, and $50 per recruit — about $700,000 — while one honest agent pays $5. Like a sable pelt that fits only one inlet of a grove, a body cannot be copied, only worn once.
